paper_citation: Forli A, Fan W, Qi KK, Yartsev MM (2025). Replay and representation dynamics in the hippocampus of freely flying bats. Nature. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09341-z
apparatus: indoor flight room, 5.6 x 5.2 x 2.5 m, with feeders

archive.name: Zenodo 15738988
archive.citation: Forli, Angelo (2025) Demo data for 'Replay and Representation Dynamics in the Hippocampus of Freely Flying Bats' [Data set]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15738988

sampling_rate.source: the Methods of Forli et al. 2025: marker positions tracked 'at a frame rate of 120 Hz' (RTLS data resampled to 120 Hz); the record's NP_Bat_Demo.m: Fs '120 Hz default'

position_span.source: the Methods of Forli et al. 2025: 'an indoor flight room (n = 4 bats, 5.6 m x 5.2 m x 2.5 m)'; the largest span of the tracked positions must lie within 20% of the 5.6 m side

speed_limit.source: Tsoar et al. 2011, PNAS 108:E718-E724: Egyptian fruit bats' commuting flight speeds were 'typically between 35 and 55 km/h', 15.3 m/s at most. No margin is added: the rodent margin of 1.5 is for headstage LEDs swinging with the head, and no source read shows a bat's head-mounted markers moving faster than its body in flight. Forli et al. 2025 states no flight speed. In a similar 5.8 x 4.6 x 2.7 m room Yartsev & Ulanovsky 2013 (Science 340:367, supplement) report a peak flight velocity of 261 +/- 15 cm/s (mean +/- s.e.m. over sessions), which this dataset's ordinary flights exceed, so it is not used

sessions.verification: Checked by hand on 2026-11-03 against the files, the record's NP_Bat_Demo.m and How to use.pdf, and the paper's Methods (Forli et al. 2025, accelerated article preview). Files: the zip's MD5 and size are those Zenodo publishes (8bbd46cf..., 3,304,325,092 bytes); its SHA-256 was computed from one full download; each of the five members read is pinned by its own SHA-256. Time: 642,724 samples every 1/120 s (the 120 Hz of the paper and of the script's Fs), from -107.4 to 5248.6 s; the spikes of the 289 units run from -12.7 to 5255.2 s, so they start inside the tracking and end 6.6 s after it. Flights: 38 (f_num), at the file's v_th of 0.5 m/s, the paper's flight threshold; one ends before the first spike. Units: 289 after the script's merges and 1 ms rule (24, 158 and 107 on probes 1 to 3). Space: r_lim is 5.8 x 5.2 x 2.3 m against the paper's 5.6 x 5.2 x 2.5 m indoor room; x from -2.84 to 2.85 m and z from 0.28 to 2.16 m lie inside r_lim, while 3.66% of tracked samples lie past its -y bound, up to 1.63 m, 0.1% of them in the file's flights (bflying).
